Stand
STAND
v. (rendering Hebrew 'āmad and qūm, and Greek histēmi, stēkō)
From Old English standan, common Germanic, from an Indo-European root *stā- that runs through Latin stare and Greek histēmi and produces an enormous family in English — stable, statute, constant, substance, resist. The root sense is fixity, and every biblical use turns on it: what stands is what has not been moved, and the question in Scripture is always what holds a thing in place.

Biblical Definition

Standing in Scripture is a matter of position rather than of posture, and there are three great senses. First, standing before God, which is the question of acceptance: who shall stand in his holy place? — he that hath clean hands and a pure heart. The wicked shall not stand in the judgment, and the blessed man of the first psalm is defined partly by where he does not stand: “nor standeth in the way of sinners” (Psa 1:1). Second, standing firm against assault, which is the language of the Christian warfare. Paul's armour passage repeats the verb like a drumbeat: “take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand” (Eph 6:13) — and it is worth noting that no ground is to be gained, only held; the whole panoply is issued so that a man may still be on his feet when the day is over. Paul's shorter charge is to the same effect: “Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong” (1Co 16:13). Third, and underneath both, the standing that is not ours at all: “Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his” (2Ti 2:19). The believer is commanded to stand precisely because he is standing on something that cannot be moved; and the same apostle who says stand fast also says let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall, so that the command and the warning are held together by grace on both sides.

Webster 1828 Definition

To be fixed in an upright position, and so in Scripture to be accepted before God, to hold ground against assault in the evil day, and to rest on the foundation of God which standeth sure — commanded of believers precisely because it is secured by God.

expand to see more

STAND, v.i. 1. To be upon the feet, as an animal; not to sit, kneel or lie.

2. To be erect, supported by the roots, as a tree or plant.

3. To remain fixed or steady; to be firm; not to fall or be overthrown. The foundation of God standeth sure. 2 Tim. 2.

4. To be placed or situated with respect to acceptance; to be admitted into the presence of. Who shall stand in his holy place? Psalm 24.

5. To stand fast; to be fixed, immovable, and unshaken. Stand fast in the faith. 1 Cor. 16. To withstand; to hold out against assault. Eph. 6.

Key Scripture

Ephesians 6:13 — "Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand."

1 Corinthians 16:13 — "Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong."

Psalm 1:1 — "Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful."

2 Timothy 2:19 — "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity."

Modern Corruption

Standing firm is recast as rigidity or as a failure of empathy, so that the one posture Scripture commands for the evil day is treated as a personality defect; and where it is retained, it is often detached from the armour that alone makes it possible.

expand to see more

The pressure on the Christian to yield is rarely argued now; it is applied through the vocabulary of manner. To hold a position is called rigidity, to decline a redefinition is called unkindness, and the whole apparatus of moral language is turned so that the man still standing appears to be the one doing harm. Eph 6 anticipates the shape of it exactly: the evil day is a day of assault, the enemies named are not flesh and blood, and the objective given is not advance but survival in position — having done all, to stand. Nothing in the passage licenses harshness; the armour includes the preparation of the gospel of peace, and the standing is done in truth and righteousness. But the passage does settle that yielding ground is defeat rather than maturity.

The opposite failure is to keep the word and lose the equipment. A man may resolve to stand fast and attempt it on temperament, conviction, or stubbornness, and Paul's point is that these will not hold in the evil day. Every piece named is either something God supplies or something God has done — His truth, His righteousness, His gospel, His word, and the shield of faith which is trust in Him — and the passage is bracketed by prayer, praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit. The Reformed instinct here is important: 2Ti 2:19 puts the foundation under the standing, and the seal on it is the Lord knoweth them that are his, not they held out. Perseverance is genuine effort resting on a preservation that is God's.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'āmad is to stand, remain, endure; qūm is to arise or be established. Greek histēmi is to set or stand, stēkō a later form meaning to stand fast, and anthistēmi is to withstand.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'āmad (H5975) — to stand, to take one's stand, to endure; some 521 occurrences, from standing before the LORD to the sun standing still upon Gibeon.

Hebrew qūm (H6965) — to arise, stand up, be established; used of a word or counsel that shall stand, as in Isa 40:8, the word of our God shall stand for ever.

Greek histēmi (G2476) — to set, place, stand; used of standing before the judgment seat and of the foundation that standeth sure.

Greek stēkō (G4739) — to stand fast, persevere; a later form derived from the perfect of histēmi, used in 1Co 16:13 and Php 1:27, stand fast in one spirit.

Greek anthistēmi (G436) — to set against, withstand, resist; used in Eph 6:13 and in Jas 4:7, resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

Usage

"Of acceptance before God: who shall stand in his holy place? (Psa 24:3); the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment (Psa 1:5)."

"Of holding ground in conflict: having done all, to stand (Eph 6:13); stand fast in the faith (1Co 16:13); stand fast in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free (Gal 5:1)."

"Of what stands independently of us: the foundation of God standeth sure (2Ti 2:19); the word of our God shall stand for ever (Isa 40:8)."
